correctness.rationale: Positive simplex and strict infected-class positivity imply a strictly decreasing susceptible-driven selection factor. Exact frequency reduction yields F_a(x)=ax(1-x)+nu(1-2x) with unique positive equilibrium y(a) strictly increasing in a. The moving equilibrium decreases, so all stationary crossings are from positive to negative frequency velocity, giving no minima and at most one maximum. Integrability of total infection yields s_infinity>0 and i_infinity=0, scalar comparison yields the explicit final frequency. Rational example has xdot(0)=37/20, while rigorous concavity forces s_infinity<1/100 and hence final x<7/10, proving exactly one peak. Symbolic and numerical checker ran successfully.

value.rationale: The per-infected mean transmissibility is the time-varying evolutionary driver of effective epidemic reproduction. This gives a full two-type temporal shape classification, an exact slow-boundary reversal mechanism, and a concrete forced peak; it prevents extrapolating published early-time increasing-mean approximations to a bounded mutating strain spectrum. The precision and sharpness of the no-multiple-peak law motivate a substantive targeted result, beyond a numerical example.
